motion.name: ease
motion.purpose: The one easing for panel, marker, rail and tone transitions.

motion.name: camera-glide
motion.value: smoothstep over the middle 64% of a screen, rest for the first and last 18%
motion.purpose: Scroll to camera pose between stops.

motion.name: camera-overview
motion.value: rotateX 57deg, rotateZ 45deg, scale 0.46 (opening) or 0.42 (closing), gap 150px or 180px
motion.purpose: Isometric view of the whole stack.

motion.name: ground-depth
motion.value: --d 0 at the opening, 0.86 to 1 across the layers, 1 at the close; tone flips to deep above 0.45
motion.purpose: Darkens the ground and scales the dot grid and glows.

motion.name: panel-in
motion.purpose: Text panel appearing near its stop.

motion.name: marker-in
motion.value: opacity 0.3s, scale 0.4 to 1 over 0.5s, delay n * 140ms + 150ms
motion.purpose: Markers on the focused plate, in order.

motion.name: plate-loop
motion.value: 8s linear infinite (some 6s or 7s), start time in --t, animating --o and --tf
motion.purpose: The looped process on each card; runs only on .is-live plates.

motion.name: riser-dots
motion.purpose: Requests going down and answers coming up.

motion.name: scroll-cue
motion.purpose: Line drawing down beside the cue label.

motion.name: reduced-motion
motion.value: flight not started; stacked document, plate animations paused
motion.purpose: Fallback for prefers-reduced-motion and no script.

components.css: .ds-hero { --bg: #fcfcfc; --fg: #171717; --muted: #6b6b6b; --accent: #0055ff; --accent-text: #0047d6; font-family: 'Host Grotesk Variable', system-ui, sans-serif; background: var(--bg); color: var(--fg); padding: 3rem 24px; } .ds-hero .ds-mark { font-size: 1.5rem; font-weight: 700; line-height: 1; margin-bottom: 2.5rem; } .ds-hero h1 { margin: 0; font-size: clamp(2.75rem, 6vw, 5.25rem); font-weight: 500; line-height: 1; letter-spacing: -0.035em; text-wrap: balance; } .ds-hero h1 span { display: block; color: var(--muted); } .ds-hero .ds-cue { display: flex; align-items: center; gap: 0.75rem; margin: 2.5rem 0 0; font-size: 0.875rem; color: var(--muted); } .ds-hero .ds-cue::before { content: ''; width: 1.5px; height: 2.25rem; background: var(--accent); transform-origin: top; animation: ds-drop 1.8s cubic-bezier(0.16, 1, 0.3, 1) infinite; } @keyframes ds-drop { 0% { transform: scaleY(0); } 60% { transform: scaleY(1); opacity: 1; } 100% { transform: scaleY(1); opacity: 0; } } @media (prefers-reduced-motion: reduce) { .ds-hero .ds-cue::before { animation: none; } }

narrative.overview:
The site is one figure: a product pulled apart into six layers (Interface, Auth, Server, Models, Cloud, Insights) and flown through by a scroll-driven camera. It opens on white paper with a large two-tone headline and the whole stack in isometric view. Scrolling moves the camera inside the stack, and the ground darkens to a deep blue-black with two soft glows and a dot grid. Every layer is the same dark card, drawn in thin lines, running its own looped process.

Text is minimal: a headline, then per layer a title, one sentence and three numbered points keyed to markers on the card. The technical edge comes from the drawings and their small labels, not from decoration. Colour beyond blue appears only as status.
keyCharacteristics: Two grounds: white paper for the opening, a deep ground for everything inside the stack.
One card style for all six plates, on either ground.
Blue is a request in motion or the active control. Green, amber, coral, violet and cyan are status only.
One typeface, Host Grotesk Variable, self-hosted.
Scroll is the only navigation device; without script or with reduced motion the page is a plain stacked document.

rules.name: The Three Tones Rule
rules.body: Colour is chosen by setting `data-tone` to `paper`, `deep` or `card` on a container, never by writing a hex in a component. The plates always carry `card`; the stage carries `paper` or `deep`, set by the camera.

rules.name: The Paper Opening Rule
rules.body: While the flight runs, the opening is white paper in every system mode. `paper` and `deep` pin `color-scheme` so form controls and scrollbars follow the ground, not the visitor's setting.

rules.name: The Depth Rule
rules.body: The ground is one continuous value `--d` from 0 (paper) to 1 (deepest), written by the camera. The base colour is `color-mix(in oklab, paper-bg, deep-ground d)`, and the dot grid (white at up to 9%, 30px pitch) and both glows scale with the same `--d`. The tone flips from `paper` to `deep` when `--d` passes 0.45, and the browser theme colour follows.

rules.name: The Meaning Only Rule
rules.body: A status colour is used only where the drawing states that thing: a check that passed, a counter filling, a 403, a model working, a row being read. Blue stays the request and the active control. No status colour is ever a layer's identity or an ornament.

rules.name: The One Face Rule
rules.body: Hierarchy comes from size, weight 500 against 400, and foreground against muted. No second typeface, no uppercase tracking, no italics.

rules.name: The Tied Shadow Rule
rules.body: A cast shadow belongs to the plate that casts it, and fades with it. A plate the camera has passed must not darken the one in focus.

rules.name: The Double Size Rule
rules.body: Plates are painted at 200% and scaled to 50% so lines and labels stay sharp when the camera tilts and zooms. Keep this when changing plate size.

dos: Do set colour through `data-tone` and the shared custom properties; add a new colour as a token in `src/styles/global.css` first.
Do keep every plate in the one card style, on any ground.
Do use blue for a request in motion and the active control, and a status colour only where the drawing states that status.
Do animate `--o` and `--tf` inside plates, and gate animations on `.is-live`.
Do keep the page readable as a stacked document without script and with reduced motion.
Do keep copy to a title, one sentence and three points per layer, with markers matching the points.
Do check both the paper and deep ground, and the system light and dark fallback, when touching stage text or lines.
donts: Don't animate `opacity` or `transform` on anything inside a plate drawing.
Don't give a layer its own colour or card style. One colour per layer was tried and rejected as too much.
Don't use status colours as decoration, or blue as a status.
Don't let the opening follow the system dark mode while the flight runs.
Don't add a second typeface or load fonts from a third party.
Don't add drop shadows to text, links or panels; depth belongs to the stack.
Don't let a cast shadow outlive the plate that casts it.
